rules.regime: 0.6 × structure + 0.4 × breadth. Structure per index (SPY, QQQ, averaged): above the latest confirmed 2W P1 and holding (> 1.5% over it) +1 · retesting it from above (−1% to +1.5%) +0.6 · uptrend under resistance (over the 200-day, under the line) +0.2 · lost a broken line −0.5 · under the line and under the 200-day −1. Breadth: the served companies' % above the 200-day and % above the 50-day, each (pct − 50) ÷ 25, averaged, clamped. Credit is a condition, not a vote: HYG's Geiger at or under −0.5 names it and takes 10 points off.
rules.stretch: the mean of four blocks, equal weight: (1) the SPY, QQQ and SMH Geigers, each placed in its own last 252 sessions (2 × percentile − 1); (2) SPY's and QQQ's daily RSI(14) and Williams %R(14), each by its own percentile the same way; (3) the VIX against its own 60-session median: read = −(VIX ÷ median − 1) ÷ 0.35, so 35% over its baseline reads −1 (fear) and 35% under reads +1 (calm); a spike is a close 35% or more over the baseline; (4) the 10-year's own Geiger (D, 3D, W bars, the Hub's formula), inverted — a hot yield is a headwind.
rules.invested: REGIME sets the base: ≥ +0.5 → 90% · ≥ +0.2 → 75% · middle → 60% · ≤ −0.2 → 40% · ≤ −0.5 → 25%; STRETCH moves it by up to 20 points (−20 × stretch); credit not confirming takes 10 off; bounded 15–100. These bases and swings are a proposal for Alan, not settled numbers.
rules.ownPast: percentiles use the last 252 sessions once available and never fewer than 100; the first sessions of the replay therefore read against a shorter own-past, and the chart marks where 252 is reached

pivot.note: ta.pivothigh(high, 2, 2) on the provider's 2W bars; a break = the first daily close above the pivot high after the bar that confirms it

macroProof.note: the chart API's /macro board carries US10Y (FMP ^TNX) with a live quote, and /candles serves its D, 3D and W bars; the Hub's /geiger board (590 served names) does not carry it, so its Geiger is rebuilt here with the Hub's formula on those bars

tree.note: a cohort's reading = the equal-weight average of its served members' Geigers (live: the Hub's seven-rung /geiger; history: the three-rung rebuild on each member's D/3D/W bars); its own percentile places the last rebuilt close among its last twelve months; growth = the median revenue growth of its members from the comps feed; cold for itself ≤ 25th percentile, good growth ≥ 15%

pullbacks.rule: from a closing high, a fall of 3% or more on closes before that high is closed over again; the RSI low is the lowest daily RSI(14) between the high and the low; the average tagged is the deepest of the 21-day (exponential), 50-, 100- and 200-day the session's low reached

leaderOnPullback.rule: over a rising 200-day with the daily RSI(14) at or under 50; sessions five or fewer apart are one visit

midpoint.rule: middling = HEAT1's replayed heat between −0.2 and +0.2 (the ladder's 50% rung); narrow leadership = the mean of the heat's own concentration and equal-weight-vs-index voters at or under −0.5; then SPY, the equal-weight S&P (RSP) and the median of our served companies over the next 20 and 60 sessions. Neighbouring sessions overlap, so the separate stretches are counted too.

coreSat.rule: The two dials set the % invested exactly as before. That % is then split in two. SATELLITE (the short-term conviction picks from the knockout and the workshop) is a quarter of the invested money while REGIME reads an uptrend (+0.2 or more), a fifth in a range or retest, a tenth in a breakdown or downtrend. CORE (the long portfolio) is the rest, half in the index sleeve and half in long-term leaders. A satellite sale goes to the core's index sleeve, not to cash: only the REGIME dial moves money between invested and cash. STRETCH decides whether new satellite buys are open (under +0.2 open; +0.2 to +0.5 only names cold for themselves; +0.5 and over trims only). The shares are ordinary core-satellite proportions put up as a proposal for Alan; the midpoint test beside this panel found no ground for tilting them by breadth.

oversold.rule: oversold = the name's Geiger sits in the lowest fifth of its own last twelve months AND reads under zero on the Hub's live scale. Growth weighs most: DESERVED when the forward year's revenue is expected to shrink, or growth is falling away (more than 10 points under the trailing twelve months and under 10%), or growth is under 5% with analysts cutting; UNDESERVED when 10% or more growth is expected and analysts are not net cutting; MIXED otherwise; a name with under $50m of revenue, or more than a fourfold jump expected, is left UNKNOWN (growth from a near-zero base says nothing). Forward growth = FMP's stored consensus revenue for the next fiscal year ÷ the reported revenue of the year before (analyst_estimates, fundamentals_history). Revisions = FMP analyst price-target raises and cuts and grade changes in the last 90 days (analyst_target_news, quarantined rows left out) — target changes, not estimate changes: the stored estimates carry one date, so true estimate revisions cannot be measured yet.

cohortBow.rule: five independent reads per cohort, each on the Geiger scale, averaged with equal weight (a missing read is named and the others carry it): (1) the equal-weight average of the members' live Geigers; (2) the same weighted by market value (FMP, the fundamentals table); (3) the Geiger of the reference fund CO1 names for the cohort, where we serve one; (4) relative strength — the members' average 63-session return minus SPY's, ±15 points = ±1; (5) the cohort against its own twelve months (2 × percentile − 1). The bow tie is (1) minus (2): above zero the average name is stronger than the giants. The three groups it makes can stand as cohorts of their own.
